## p186 A1/A2 — Earlier Russian and Polish traffic instruction

**Sources on this page:** p186 A1, p186 A2.

<a id="edition-cases-context-p186-p186-a1a2--earlier-russian-and-polish-traffic-instruction"></a>


[Source image](../sources/excerpts/childs_p186_A.png)

**Status:** Earlier corpus reading, source-checked under `Nov13-15b`.
**Present source and coordinate review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

Norbert's [comment 53, 3 May 2017](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-878079)
identifies this earlier transmission and says it had already been deciphered
by the Lasry team. Both its known status and that attribution are retained.

<a id="source-p186-a1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-context-p186-part-1--richi-170"></a>

### Part 1 — RICHI-170

The 170 received positions contain three printed erasures. The raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
RUSS?SCHENUN?POLNHEEREVERKEHRVOLLERFASSENWICHTIGESBESONDAUSPOLNVERKEHRUEBEROHLSTA?ION
```

</details>

Filling received indices 147, 148 and 149 with `DAA` gives the displayed body
without changing any known coordinate. This is a source-supported word
proposal under the fixed key, not an observation of the missing glyphs.

<a id="source-p186-a2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-context-p186-part-2--richi-174"></a>

### Part 2 — RICHI-174

Two ambiguous printed glyphs are kept unknown in the conservative layer.
It fixes **80 of 87 positions**:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
VERZIFFERTFUNKENSOWEITFERNSCHREIBERVERBDGNICHTARBEITETXRESTSCHRIFTLICH?ACHCHEF??1???1?X
```

</details>

The repeated known numeral `1` belongs to this reading. It cannot simply be
copied into the [p187b](187.md#edition-cases-p187b) suffix, which has a different length and
different shared-cell constraints. This published-key layer supplies no
additional numerical label.

<a id="edition-cases-context-p186-conditional-shared-key-reference-labels"></a>

#### Conditional shared-key reference labels

The [shared Nov13–15b interpretation](../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/coverage.md)
(`XX=Q`, `VG=2`) fixes **82 of 87 positions** in the conservative source,
with the administrative ending **`CHEF??1??212X`**. Its number remains
unidentified.

The two added digits use intact `VG` pairs at plaintext positions 83 and 85,
from source positions `[173, 10]` and `[64, 107]` (zero-based). The source
masks at 20 and 29 remain, and the coordinate-edit cost is unchanged. These
labels inherit the shared-key interpretation; five positions remain unresolved.

<a id="edition-cases-context-p186-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German — body interpretation; the final ellipsis omits the unresolved administrative ending shown in Part 2:**

> Russischen und poln. Heereverkehr voll erfassen. Wichtiges, besond. aus poln.
> Verkehr, ueber OHL-Station verziffert funken. Soweit Fernschreiber-Verbdg.
> nicht arbeitet, Rest schriftlich. [Nachchef] […]

**Meaning:** Monitor Russian and Polish army traffic comprehensively. Radio
important material, especially Polish traffic, in cipher through the Supreme
Army Command station. Where the teleprinter connection is not working, send
the rest in writing. The administrative ending remains incomplete.

Word divisions and punctuation are editorial. Part 1's readable completion
uses three erasure fills supported by corresponding words in [p187](187.md#edition-cases-p187).
The source's abbreviated `BESOND` and `HEEREVERKEHR` are retained here; this
transmission is not identical to p187/p187b.

<a id="edition-cases-context-p186-evidence"></a>

### Evidence

The header is `SU v LP (06.33 a.m., November 13th); 20.50 (13/11); 2 TLE`.
The records are printed p186 / PDF page 189. Their full transcriptions and
earlier credit are in [the source record](../data/reviews/p186_chi_parallel.json).
The [conservative source audit](../experiments/source_followup/p186_source_and_suffix_delta.json)
contains the two glyph masks, the three proposed fills and exact word maps.

```sh
python3 experiments/source_followup/audit_p186.py --verify
python3 experiments/nov13_joint_completion/verify_coverage.py --verify
```

## p186 B1 — Ober Ost troop-movement proposal, conditional obliteration exclusion

**Edition context:** Ober Ost troop movements: a conditional reading across two obliterations.

<a id="edition-cases-military-oberost-troop-movement-obliterations-ober-ost-troop-movements-a-conditional-reading-across-two-obliterations"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The first part of p186 B proposes troop movements within the Ober Ost territory. This reading depends on explicitly excluding two obliterated group-width regions. The surviving second part independently describes soldiers wanting to travel home without authorization; it is published in the [native companion edition](#edition-cases-military-home-departures-baltic-transport-p186-b2).

<a id="source-p186-b1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-oberost-troop-movement-obliterations-p186-b1"></a>

### p186 B1

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — retain both five-mask regions in the 318-position composite layout; diagnostic only:**

```text
?0AMOVBM1ZRPVZR??LS?R5FDX?TXZO0SPX?5ICFJA??H?O6??R?K1CC6XP?PX?TK6V?MXV?I?F?Z0XENUF?6FVTPVC?EOHEPE??E?ZBIMA?INTCGMG?III???C?GZSELW?LUNMOB5XG?IMEDGS?EZ?EDNIBCLDP
```

**Raw output — conditional 308-coordinate frame after ten masked-layout-slot exclusions; 150 of 154 positions fixed:**

```text
GENXGOUVXWARSCHAUXZ0FORTX?MX1AXNRR6?1X15XGENXVX10X11XISTANOBOSTGEDRAHTETXXESWIRDVORGESCHLX?ENXTRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG?NINNERHALBDESOBEROSTGEBIETSVORZUNEHMENXX
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame, one observed-coordinate substitution and two source-mask fills; 152 of 154 positions fixed:**

```text
GENXGOUVXWARSCHAUXZ0FORTX?MX1AXNRR6?1X15XGENXVX10X11XISTANOBOSTGEDRAHTETXXESWIRDVORGESCHLAGENXTRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNGENINNERHALBDESOBEROSTGEBIETSVORZUNEHMENXX
```

</details>

All indices below refer to the 318-position composite source layout. The observed substitution is **88 D→V**. The two source-mask fills are **91 Y-like glyph→X** and **137 C/G-shaped glyph→G**. The ten excluded masks do not receive guessed coordinate values and are not counted as fills.

**Readable German — conditional frame and explicitly priced changes; opaque fields retained:**

> Gen. Gouv. Warschau. Z0FORT. ?MX1AXNRR6?1X15XGENXVX10X11 ist an OBOST gedrahtet. Es wird vorgeschlagen, Truppenverschiebungen innerhalb des Oberostgebiets vorzunehmen.

**Meaning:** The body addresses GEN GOUV WARSCHAU, says that the referenced item has been wired to OBOST, and proposes troop movements within the Ober Ost territory. Z0FORT and the opening reference remain opaque literal fields. The text is a proposal, not evidence that the movements occurred.

The two remaining unknowns come from unresolved square cells: VG at plaintext index 25 and AF at index 35. The AF position is coupled to p186 C1 index 11; it must differ from GA, which is shared by p186 B2 index 109 and C1 index 9. All indices are zero-based, and none of these reference labels is historically assigned. The published Nov13–15b key is unchanged; its nonhistorical injective completion witness verifies compatibility without selecting historical numeral labels. Z0FORT is not silently normalized to SOFORT, and the reference `?MX1AXNRR6?1X15XGENXVX10X11` remains literal. The phrase “ist an OBOST gedrahtet” reports earlier transmission of the referenced item; the following sentence proposes movements. Neither establishes that troop movements occurred.

<a id="edition-cases-military-oberost-troop-movement-obliterations-source-geometry-and-its-limits"></a>

### Source geometry and its limits

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p186 excerpt](../experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/sources/p186_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/inputs.json) · [Position certificates and controls](../experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/certificates.json)

**Source transcription — header:** `B) NKJ v LP (06.23 a.m., November 13th); FUER WAU 07.00 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-308`

The fourth ciphertext row has two heavily obliterated regions between GFDXG and the following C/G-ambiguous group. They occupy two ordinary group columns, but five separate original glyphs cannot be counted in either region. The disclosed **318-position composite layout** consists of **308 individually transcribed positions plus two regions modeled as five masks each**. It is not a claim that 318 separate original coordinate letters remain visible.

**Conditional interpretation — source-row layout with five inferred masks for each obliterated group column:**

```text
GFDXG ????? ????? FGCGA AFGFA GVXVD DXXXF AFFVF
```

The C/G-shaped glyph in FGCGA is transcribed C and masked; its ambiguity is independent of the two obliterated regions. The Y-like glyph in XYVXX is also masked. All other positions are retained in source order.

The primary frame excludes the ten modeled masks at composite source indices 125–134, yielding the advertised 308 coordinates. This costs **ten masked-layout-slot exclusions**. It deletes no observed coordinate. The agreement with the heading supports examining this geometry, but neither the heading nor a readable result proves that the obliterations were intended cancellations.

The certificate preserves all four choices: retain both regions (318 positions), exclude either region alone (313 positions), and exclude both (308 positions). Both odd-length controls explicitly identify their unpaired intermediate coordinate and its source index; their final coordinate is not silently discarded as source evidence. The two single-region controls happen to have identical streams because both regions are entirely masked.

<a id="edition-cases-military-oberost-troop-movement-obliterations-native-date-context-and-numerical-labels"></a>

### Native date context and numerical labels

The unchanged field `GENXVX10X11XISTANOBOSTGEDRAHTET` provides a separate
contextual check on DD, which carries the published label 1. Within the
same conditional obliteration frame, the two final month labels use the
original **DD** pairs at composite source indices **170/122** and **305/6**.
All ten coordinates of `10X11` are observed; none uses a word repair or
mask fill. The [joint verifier](../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
replays the complete field from the source transcription.

If `10X11` is a day/month date, 11 is the only valid repeated-digit month,
so this supports retaining **numerical DD=1** independently of the p193
award. The date reading is explicitly conditional, and the larger reference
remains opaque. This argument changes no source coordinate or fixed-label
count and does not resolve the obliteration geometry.

<a id="edition-cases-military-oberost-troop-movement-obliterations-exact-account"></a>

### Exact account

The separate [p193 award-class interpretation](../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md)
propagates `VG=2` to the opening field, giving `2MX1AXNRR6?1`.
This raises the conditional label count to **153/154** but leaves the
opening opaque. It supplies no additional ordinary word or source repair.

| Quantity | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| New physical source records | 1 |
| Individually transcribed positions | 308 |
| Added layout masks for two obliterated group columns | 10 |
| Composite layout positions | 318 |
| Conditional analyzed coordinates / plaintext positions | 308 / 154 |
| Fixed conditional raw / edited labels | 150 / 152 |
| Excluded layout masks / excluded observed coordinates | 10 / 0 |
| Observed-coordinate substitutions / source-mask fills | 1 / 2 |
| Inserted coordinates or reordered source positions | 0 |

These counts exclude the already separate native second part. The certificate's `printed_source_slots` is 308, while `composite_layout_slots` is 318; `source_deletions` counts the ten modeled-mask exclusions, with `observed_coordinate_deletions` separately fixed at zero. This prevents the group-width model from being represented as ten legible original letters.

<a id="edition-cases-military-oberost-troop-movement-obliterations-evidence-credit-and-reproduction"></a>

### Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

[Earlier OCR candidates](../experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/prior_candidates.json) and the [original OCR snapshot](../experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/ocr_snapshot.json) remain separately frozen. The new source analysis does not treat an OCR token count as a historical received length.

```sh
python experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/verify.py --verify
python experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

Verification checks every source/model index, the four control frames, all position domains, each proposed change, exact readable-label preservation, an injective global completion witness, unchanged key provenance and the optional original-PDF crop pixels. A successful round-trip establishes compatibility with the declared exclusion model, not a unique historical reading or cancellation intent.

## Wishing to travel home and uncertainty over Baltic transport

**Sources on this page:** p186 B2, p186 C1.

<a id="edition-cases-military-home-departures-baltic-transport-wishing-to-travel-home-and-uncertainty-over-baltic-transport"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two native source bodies describe soldiers wishing to travel home without authorization and transport difficulty linked to uncertainty in the Baltic Sea. The second begins an incomplete statement about Graf Goltz. One damaged source glyph in that body is retained as unknown; its unchanged edited reading requires one explicit source-mask fill. The shared unknown GA cell remains globally coupled across their separate references. Missing context and abbreviated source spellings stay explicit.

<a id="source-p186-b2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-home-departures-baltic-transport-p186-b2"></a>

### p186 B2

**Source transcription — header:** `B) NKJ v LP (06.23 a.m., November 13th); FUER WAU 07.00 2 TLE; 2 TL RICHI-242`

**Readable German:** based on the unchanged raw output.

> Die Schwierigkeiten, dass Mannschaften eigenmaechtig nach Hause fahren wollen, sind ueberall die gleichen. OHL. RM 1A Nr. 11?01 Geh. Op.

**Meaning:** The second part states that the difficulty is the same everywhere: soldiers want to travel home on their own authority. It closes with OHL and an unresolved office reference. It reports the problem; it does not itself authorize those departures.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
DIESCHWIERIGKEITENXDASSMANNSCHAFTENEIGENMAECHTIGNACHHAUSEFAHRENWOLLENXSINDUEBERALLDIEGLEICHENXOHLXRMX1AXNRX11?01XGEHXOPXX
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits:**

- All 242 printed coordinates are preserved and decode without repairs. The earlier OCR separated the first row and omitted additional source material; those OCR defects are not historical ciphertext losses.
- The heading explicitly identifies this as part 2. The independently handled first part has two group-width obliterations and a conditional exclusion model; this native part does not rely on that model.
- The literal reference 11?01 retains one globally coupled unknown square cell. No historical file number or date is inferred.
- The unknown in 11?01 is the same GA square cell as the first unknown in p186 C1's DRTRM1A?5?; both must have the same unresolved label. The second unknown in that C1 field is AF and must have a different label.

<a id="source-p186-c1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-home-departures-baltic-transport-p186-c1"></a>

### p186 C1

**Source transcription — header:** `C) KOW v LP (06.26 a.m., November 13th); 17.40 (13/11) 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-182; (Continued)`

**Readable German:** based on the edited output with one disclosed source-mask fill.

> Zu DRTRM1A?5?. ABTRSPRT z. Zt. wegen unklarer Lage in Ostsee UNMOGLCH. Gen. Graf Goltz hat jedoch VORBEREITG

**Meaning:** This first part concerns transport that is currently described as impossible because the situation in the Baltic Sea is unclear. It then begins a statement about preparations associated with the literal name and title GEN GRAF GOLTZ. The statement is incomplete in this source body, so no completed plan or action is supplied.

<details>
<summary>Raw and edited decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
ZUDRTRM1A?5?XABTRSPRTXZXZTWEGENUNKLARERLAGEINOSTSEEUNMOGLCHXG?NGRAFGOLTZHATJEDOCHVORBEREITG
```

**Edited output** — the E in `GEN` depends on the disclosed F interpretation of the damaged source glyph.

```text
ZUDRTRM1A?5?XABTRSPRTXZXZTWEGENUNKLARERLAGEINOSTSEEUNMOGLCHXGENGRAFGOLTZHATJEDOCHVORBEREITG
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits:**

- All 182 source slots are preserved. In the third cipher row, the first glyph of the seventh group has an F/R-like outline with an attached lower-right diagonal. The [original-PDF crop](../experiments/home_departures_baltic_transport/sources/p186_C1_damaged_glyph.png) supports masking it as `?FAFF`, without assigning the competing literal letter R. At zero-based source index 110 it combines with source index 64 to give pair `X?` and plaintext position 61, whose domain is `234789CEGIQTY`.
- The edited E in `GEN` fills source index 110 with F. The main reading therefore has 88 fixed raw positions and 89 fixed edited positions out of 91, with no observed-coordinate substitutions and one source-mask fill. The certificate retains the former F interpretation as an explicit sensitivity assumption: 89 raw positions and no fill. It is excluded from observed-source totals; the change records uncertainty, not a repair-cost reduction or a new recovery.
- The scan labels two parts and prints “Continued,” but only this first body is included here. No missing continuation is reconstructed from context.
- DRTRM1A?5?, ABTRSPRT, UNMOGLCH and VORBEREITG are retained literally. The English meaning interprets the abbreviated transport statement; no missing I, vowel or grammatical ending is added to the decoded stream.
- The two question marks in the opening reference come from different unresolved square cells; their labels remain globally injective rather than being independently guessed.
- The literal name GRAF GOLTZ is not used to add a first name or identify a historical biography.

<a id="edition-cases-military-home-departures-baltic-transport-evidence-and-credit"></a>

### Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For a partial output, an injective global completion of the square and residual source masks supplies an explicitly nonhistorical round-trip witness. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/home_departures_baltic_transport/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A round-trip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.
